note: Attacker-controlled input bytes of the \uXXXX escape sequence are consumed as hex digits and accumulated into tok->ucs_char / tok->st_pos inside json_tokener_state_escape_unicode.
Four hex digits complete the first unicode escape; the decoded value is tok->ucs_char (0xD83D for the crafted input).
The decoded escape 0xD83D is classified as a high surrogate.
The high surrogate value is remembered in tok->got_hi_surrogate while the parser looks ahead for the low surrogate escape.
Lookahead finds '\u' after the high surrogate, so the parser advances into a second escape sequence (the low surrogate).
After consuming the single hex digit '1' of the second escape, the input is exhausted (char_offset == len), so PEEK_CHAR fails and control reaches the cleanup block.

Root cause: although the second (low surrogate) escape is incomplete - input ran out in the middle of it - the cleanup unconditionally treats the pending high surrogate as unpaired and decides to emit a replacement char.
Sink: the 3-byte UTF-8 replacement character (0xEF 0xBF 0xBD) is appended into tok->pb even though the unicode escape never completed, corrupting handling of the incomplete sequence.
